chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, from Salih ibn Abi Himad, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from his father, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdullah, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) narrated:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Sheep, when they face you, face you [are profitable], and when they turn away, face you [are still profitable]. Cows, when they face you, face you, and when they turn away, turn away [are not profitable]. Camels are the reins of the devils; when they face you, they turn away, and when they turn away, they turn away. Their goodness does not come except from the unlucky side.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, then who should keep them?' He said: 'Then where are the wretched sinners?' Salih said: And Isma'il ibn Mihran recited a poem: 'It is wealth, were it not for the scarcity of lowering [price] around it, so whoever wishes can keep it, and whoever wishes can sell it.'

key_terms.أَعْنَانُ الشَّيَاطِينِ: Reins of the devils (idiom for being troublesome or costly)

ai.seo_question: What is the Prophet's view on the profitability of camels compared to sheep and cows?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the varying degrees of economic prudence in livestock, a common theme in early Islamic agrarian society. The Prophet’s metaphor of camels as the 'reins of the devils' highlights their stubbornness and high maintenance, suggesting that retaining them requires more effort than reward, thus appealing to the 'wretched' or those lacking discernment. This classification serves as a practical ethical guideline for wealth management, emphasizing efficiency and ease in trade.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-106 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Kufy quoted Salih ibn Abi Himad, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Mihran, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Abil Miqdam, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Sheep are profitable whether they face you or turn around . Cows are also profitable whether they face you or turn around. However, camels are from the regions of the satans. They cause a loss whether they face you or turn around. They have no use except for their unfortunate owners who worry that they may get harmed.’ The Prophet (MGB) was asked, ‘O Prophet of God! Who should then raise camels?’ The Prophet (MGB) replied, ‘Unfortunate owners!’”
Salih ibn Abi Himad added, ‘And then Isma’il ibn Mihran recited a poem in this respect.’”
